title: Stored XSS on public news detail page via quote-boundary bypass of event-handler sanitizer
description: News article content is sanitized with `strip_tags()` followed by a regular expression intended to remove inline event handlers. Because `strip_tags()` preserves attributes on allowed tags and the regex only matches handlers preceded by whitespace or `/`, an attacker who can author news (any admin) can inject a live event handler by closing a preceding attribute with a quote — e.g. `<div title="x"onmouseover="alert(document.domain)">`. The payload is stored raw in the database and emitted unescaped inside the public article body, so it executes in the browser of every visitor (including unauthenticated guests) who interacts with the article.
impact: An admin-authored article becomes a persistent XSS vector on a public, unauthenticated page. Triggering requires only hovering over the injected content (or, with the `autofocus`/`onfocus` variant, no interaction at all). Impact includes session/token theft (CSRF tokens are exposed in the DOM), execution of attacker JavaScript in the origin of the news portal, content defacement, and drive-by actions on behalf of any visitor — students, lecturers, and administrators — who views the article.

Two layers are involved, and both share the same defective pattern. **At store time** — `NewsController::sanitizeNewsContent()`: ```php title=controllers/NewsController.php $allowedTags = '

The handler-stripping regex requires the handler name to be preceded by a whitespace character or `/`. In `title="x"onmouseover="alert(1)"`, the `onmouseover` token is preceded by `"` (the closing quote of the previous attribute), which the regex does not match, so the handler survives. remediation_steps: Replace the tag-based `strip_tags()` + regex sanitizer with a well-tested HTML sanitization library (e.g. HTML Purifier with an explicit allow-list of tags and attributes, no event handlers and no `style`), applied on input and treated as authoritative on output. Enforce a strict attribute allow-list rather than attempting to blacklist `on*` handlers via regex. Additionally, ensure the render path never emits stored content raw: either sanitize with the library at render time or escape by default and only re-introduce markup through the sanitizer. Deploy a strict Content Security Policy and remove `unsafe-inline` from `script-src` so that inline handlers are refused even if injected. Apply the same fix to every place content is stored or rendered.

code_locations.label: Defective handler-stripping regex in store-path sanitizer
Same defective sanitizer at render time; result emitted raw

fix_pr_body:
## Summary

The news sanitizer attempts to strip inline event handlers with a regex that only matches handlers preceded by whitespace or `/`. Since `strip_tags()` preserves attributes on allowed tags, closing a preceding attribute with a quote (`title="x"onmouseover=...`) places the handler after a `"` and bypasses the regex. The render path repeats the same logic and emits the surviving markup raw, producing stored XSS on a public page.

## Rationale

- Regex-based blacklisting of `on*` handlers is unreliable; a strict allow-list of tags and attributes is required.
- Sanitization must be authoritative at render time (or output must be escaped by default).
- A library such as HTML Purifier with an attribute allow-list eliminates this class of bypass.

## Change

Replace the `strip_tags` + regex sanitizer with an allow-list HTML sanitizer and escape any content that has not been sanitized. See the suggested code locations.
